conclusions: Integrated-centroid and storage-constrained quasi-steady closures are numerically well behaved on the frozen cohort but are not broadly superior to the standard LARE closure.
Their pooled L3 improvement is driven by the high-state S3_B1_F3 case; all three S2 cases worsen on both RMS and maximum long-interface flux error.
No storage-only closure tested in A2 or A2B satisfies the frozen broad-support rule.
The preregistered state-augmentation gate is activated. The next experiment may add one physically interpretable gradient or moment coordinate, but may not fit an empirical correction.
